subject: FinTrail post-call: deployment fit, throughput & latency SLOs
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Liam Parker <liam.parker@fintrail.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@fintrail.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — deployment fit, throughput and latency targets

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap while the details are fresh and to confirm next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you shared
- High tail latency for your risk-scoring microservice during peak batching windows; p95 experienced ~450ms currently and spikes to p99 > 1s.
- Need predictable latency for real-time transaction scoring (under regulatory SLAs) and throughput peaks during market open (~10x baseline).
- Sensitive PII in prompts — SOC 2 + VPC connectivity are hard requirements.

Goals we agreed on
- Target production SLO: p95 tail latency <= 150–200ms for 16-token classification/generation for the majority of workflows; p99 mitigation plan for burst traffic.
- Sustained throughput target for Phase 1: ~500 req/s (classification-style requests), with burst capacity to ~2k req/s for up to 5 minutes.
- Private deployment behind customer VPC (initially Private control plane in our managed offer) to satisfy compliance.

Technical notes / hypotheses
- Workload shape: many short requests (8–32 tokens), some longer conversational sessions with context caching. KV cache will reduce per-token cost for sessions.
- Model fit: recommended a middle-sized open model (70B-class with int8/quantized profile) for balance of latency and quality; we can test both a distilled 16B variant and a 70B quantized path in the PoC.
- Topology options: dedicated GPU pool (private) with autoscaling + cross-region fallback for availability. We sketched H100-backed instances for throughput runs and A10/A30 for steady-state cheaper capacity.

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Mateo (me): capture the mutual action plan and share this recap + a proposed timeline (today).
- Liam / Priya: share a one-week sample of traffic (anonymized) and a short list of golden prompts + acceptance examples (ASAP).
- Jasmine: produce a short 1-page sketch (topology options, sizing hypotheses, quantization tradeoffs) by EOD Wednesday.
- Grace: prepare a trial onboarding checklist and procurement contacts for a pilot (end of week).

Attachments: I’m attaching a requirements workbook you can fill (fintrail_poc_requirements.xlsx) and will include Jasmine’s topology PNG after she drafts it.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample traffic.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — deployment fit, throughput and latency targets

Thanks Mateo — good notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 500 req/s is an average across our core risk scorer endpoints; peak during market open is closer to 1.8k req/s for ~10 minutes.
- Typical payloads are small JSONs with 8–24 tokens for the extracted text, but we also have a streaming path used by our fraud ops team that can be up to 128 tokens.
- SOC 2 + VPC peering are mandatory. On-prem is possible but we'd prefer a private-managed deployment to start.

We attached a lightweight traffic export (anonymized) and a filled sheet for baseline numbers.

Liam
Liam Parker
VP Product, FinTrail

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Liam Parker <liam.parker@fintrail.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2028 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Technical follow-up — topology sketch & sizing suggestions

Hi Liam / Mateo —

Following Mateo's summary, attached is a short topology sketch and sizing notes (see inline below). I put conservative numbers so we can tighten them once we ingest your sample traffic.

Recommended approach (Phase 1 PoC)
- Private-managed deployment (customer VPC peering) with dedicated GPU pool.
- Primary: 4 x H100 nodes (for concurrency-heavy worker pool) for burst windows.
- Warm steady-state: 8 x A10G-equivalent nodes for cost-effective throughput for the 500 req/s baseline.
- Autoscaling policy: scale-up threshold at 65% util, aggressive scale-down delay during short peaks to avoid thrash.

Model & quantization profile
- Baseline: redwood-llama2-70b-q8 (quantized int8 path) for quality parity. Expect lower throughput than smaller variants but better decisioning quality.
- Cost-conscious path: redwood-llama2-16b-int8 distill for faster p95 and much higher qps.
- For streaming or long context sessions: enable KV cache pinned to session routing to reduce repeated decoding for context.

Latency & batching guidance (initial)
- Optimize for low-latency single-request paths: target p95 < 180ms for short responses by configuring small micro-batches (max batch 8) for latency-critical endpoints.
- For high-throughput non-latency-critical scoring jobs, use larger batch windows (batch size 16–32) with a 20–50ms wait window to increase token throughput efficiency.

Fallback & resilience
- Model fallback chain: 70B-q8 -> 16B-int8 -> smaller distilled variant to preserve availability if capacity constrained.
- Regional fallback to a secondary region (read-only) with documented cold start mitigation.

I'll attach the PNG topology (redwood-deploy-topology.png) and a one-page sizing table. Mateo — happy to turn this into a slide if FinTrail wants a short decision deck.

-Jasmine
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-deploy-topology.png (image/png)]

- Trial capacity: we can provision a staged pilot (2 H100 + 4 A10-equivalents) for up to 30 days.

If you can share the contact for procurement and the InfoSec lead, I’ll get the paperwork moving. Proposed timeline: provisioning within 5 business days of a signed MPA.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
